register: Standard defense and diplomatic-history term, normally plural when referring to a state’s weapons-testing program or the practice generally.
trap: In this Cold War context, essai means a weapons test; test nucléaire can also describe a technical test involving nuclear technology and is less historically specific.
example_tl: Les essais nucléaires atmosphériques ont exposé des populations éloignées aux retombées radioactives, alors même que les gouvernements minimisaient les risques sanitaires.
example_en: Atmospheric nuclear tests exposed remote populations to radioactive fallout even as governments played down the health risks.
cloze: {{c1::Les essais nucléaires}} atmosphériques ont exposé des populations éloignées aux retombées radioactives, alors même que les gouvernements minimisaient les risques sanitaires.
note: Old_back is accurate. Self-review retained the conventional plural, made the weapons-testing sense explicit, and replaced a needlessly literary past anterior with an idiomatic imperfect.

register: Standard strategic-studies term for military forces and weapons that are not nuclear, biological, or chemical.
trap: Here conventionnelles means non-nuclear and related non-WMD forces, not forces that are merely usual, traditional, or compliant with a convention.
example_tl: Les forces conventionnelles massées en Europe centrale devaient pouvoir ralentir une offensive sans déclencher immédiatement un échange nucléaire entre les superpuissances.
example_en: The conventional forces massed in Central Europe were expected to slow an offensive without immediately triggering a nuclear exchange between the superpowers.
cloze: {{c1::Les forces conventionnelles}} massées en Europe centrale devaient pouvoir ralentir une offensive sans déclencher immédiatement un échange nucléaire entre les superpuissances.
note: Old_back is accurate. Self-review defined the term by its strategic contrast and avoided implying that conventional necessarily means technologically obsolete.

register: Neutral-formal diplomatic and security term for a deliberate reduction in the intensity or danger of a confrontation.
trap: The established noun is désescalade; mechanically importing English de-escalation as dé-escalation or désescalation is unnecessary in standard France French.
example_tl: La désescalade exigeait le retrait progressif des missiles, un calendrier vérifiable et des canaux capables de prévenir tout malentendu susceptible de relancer la confrontation.
example_en: De-escalation required the gradual withdrawal of the missiles, a verifiable timetable, and channels capable of preventing any misunderstanding that could reignite the confrontation.
cloze: {{c1::La désescalade}} exigeait le retrait progressif des missiles, un calendrier vérifiable et des canaux capables de prévenir tout malentendu susceptible de relancer la confrontation.
note: Old_back is accurate. Self-review replaced a vague reference to hostile interpretation with a concrete escalation risk and excluded réduction des tensions because it need not entail reciprocal action.

register: Standard scientific, historical, and policy term for radioactive material descending after a nuclear explosion; the alternative is common but less physically explicit.
trap: Retombées can mean beneficial or harmful consequences figuratively, but retombées radioactives denotes the physical contamination and is normally plural.
example_tl: Les retombées radioactives ont contaminé des pâturages situés à des milliers de kilomètres du site, révélant le caractère transfrontalier des essais atmosphériques.
example_en: Radioactive fallout contaminated pastures thousands of kilometers from the site, revealing the transboundary nature of atmospheric testing.
cloze: {{c1::Les retombées radioactives}} ont contaminé des pâturages situés à des milliers de kilomètres du site, révélant le caractère transfrontalier des essais atmosphériques.
note: Self-review replaced old_back’s less precise retombées nucléaires with the standard physical term and retained the legacy form only as a contextually valid alternative.

register: Established strategic and journalistic metaphor for extended deterrence supplied by a nuclear power to its allies.
trap: A parapluie nucléaire is a deterrent guarantee, not a physical shield that intercepts missiles; défense antimissile names the latter concept.
example_tl: Le parapluie nucléaire américain rassurait les alliés européens, mais alimentait aussi le débat sur leur dépendance stratégique envers Washington.
example_en: The American nuclear umbrella reassured European allies, but it also fueled debate about their strategic dependence on Washington.
cloze: {{c1::Le parapluie nucléaire}} américain rassurait les alliés européens, mais alimentait aussi le débat sur leur dépendance stratégique envers Washington.
note: Old_back is accurate. Self-review defined the metaphor through extended deterrence and explicitly separated it from missile defense.

register: Neutral-formal analytical metaphor for a relationship without open war but still marked by hostility, mistrust, and little cooperation.
trap: Paix froide describes a condition and is not another name for la guerre froide, the historically specific geopolitical confrontation.
example_tl: Après l’accord, une paix froide s’est installée entre les deux États, sans coopération durable ni véritable normalisation de leurs relations diplomatiques.
example_en: After the agreement, a cold peace settled between the two states, without lasting cooperation or any genuine normalization of their diplomatic relations.
cloze: Après l’accord, {{c1::une paix froide}} s’est installée entre les deux États, sans coopération durable ni véritable normalisation de leurs relations diplomatiques.
note: Old_back gives the right phrase but capitalizes it unnecessarily. Self-review used an indefinite article in the example because it describes a newly established condition.

register: Neutral and direct for facing an adversary, danger, or difficult reality; faire face à is slightly less combative and equally standard.
trap: Confronter is not a blanket equivalent of English confront: French normally confronts two accounts or confronte quelqu’un à a fact, but affronte a danger.
example_tl: Les dirigeants américains ont dû affronter un risque croissant de guerre nucléaire tout en maintenant un canal discret avec Moscou.
example_en: American leaders had to confront a growing risk of nuclear war while maintaining a discreet channel with Moscow.
cloze: Les dirigeants américains ont dû {{c1::affronter}} un risque croissant de guerre nucléaire tout en maintenant un canal discret avec Moscou.
note: The source is polysemous; this card selects confronting a danger or difficult reality. Self-review replaced the less idiomatic possibilité with risque and retained only an alternative that fits unchanged.

register: Neutral-formal and standard in policy prose; s’élever contre is more rhetorical and emphasizes publicly voicing opposition.
trap: Unlike transitive English oppose, French requires the pronominal verb and à: s’opposer à une mesure, not opposer une mesure in this sense.
example_tl: Plusieurs diplomates se sont opposés à l’installation de nouveaux missiles, estimant qu’elle réduirait dangereusement le temps disponible pour toute décision.
example_en: Several diplomats opposed the deployment of new missiles, judging that it would dangerously reduce the time available for any decision.
cloze: Plusieurs diplomates {{c1::se sont opposés à}} l’installation de nouveaux missiles, estimant qu’elle réduirait dangereusement le temps disponible pour toute décision.
note: Old_back gives the right verb but omits its governed preposition. Self-review verified that the alternative can replace the main expression in this public-policy context after normal inflection.

register: Neutral-formal geopolitical and policy expression, often implying that an actor adopts another power’s position or strategic line.
trap: When one actor adopts another’s position or model, French conventionally uses sur; avec can express coordination, so it should not replace sur mechanically here.
example_tl: Après le coup d’État, le nouveau régime s’est aligné sur la politique de Moscou afin d’obtenir des armes, des crédits et une protection diplomatique.
example_en: After the coup, the new regime aligned itself with Moscow’s policy in order to obtain weapons, credit, and diplomatic protection.
cloze: Après le coup d’État, le nouveau régime {{c1::s’est aligné sur}} la politique de Moscou afin d’obtenir des armes, des crédits et une protection diplomatique.
note: Old_back gives the right pronominal verb but omits sur. Dictionary review confirmed the policy-conformity frame; self-review added politique to make that selected sense unmistakable.

register: Neutral-formal intelligence and policing verb when a service covertly penetrates an organization or network.
trap: A service can infiltrer un mouvement directly, whereas an agent who enters it covertly commonly s’infiltre dans le mouvement; the constructions shift the viewpoint.
example_tl: Les services de renseignement ont infiltré le mouvement étudiant afin d’identifier ses réseaux de financement et d’anticiper ses campagnes contre le régime.
example_en: The intelligence services infiltrated the student movement to identify its funding networks and anticipate its campaigns against the regime.
cloze: Les services de renseignement {{c1::ont infiltré}} le mouvement étudiant afin d’identifier ses réseaux de financement et d’anticiper ses campagnes contre le régime.
note: Old_back supplies only the bare transitive lemma. Self-review selected the institutional transitive viewpoint, preferred services de renseignement, and kept the agent-centered reflexive construction as a contrast.

register: Neutral and widely used for withstanding pressure, coercion, occupation, or an adversary; the complement is introduced by à.
trap: French résister is indirect: résister à la pression. English resist and Spanish resistir take direct objects, a strong cross-language interference risk.
example_tl: Malgré la censure, des rédactions clandestines ont résisté à la pression du parti et continué de documenter les arrestations politiques.
example_en: Despite censorship, underground newsrooms resisted pressure from the party and continued to document political arrests.
cloze: Malgré la censure, des rédactions clandestines {{c1::ont résisté à}} la pression du parti et continué de documenter les arrestations politiques.
note: Old_back omits the governed preposition. Self-review kept the card because the indirect construction remains a live production trap even though the verb itself is common.

register: Neutral-formal diplomatic and economic-policy construction for subjecting a state, regime, or trade category to an embargo.
trap: English freely verbalizes embargo; standard formal French normally uses imposer un embargo à or mettre sous embargo rather than a bare verb.
example_tl: Après l’invasion, plusieurs États ont imposé un embargo au régime, mais des intermédiaires commerciaux ont continué d’acheminer des composants stratégiques.
example_en: After the invasion, several states imposed an embargo on the regime, but commercial intermediaries continued to transport strategic components.
cloze: Après l’invasion, plusieurs États {{c1::ont imposé un embargo}} {{c1::au}} régime, mais des intermédiaires commerciaux ont continué d’acheminer des composants stratégiques.
note: Old_back’s mettre sous embargo is valid, but self-review chose the more institutional support-verb frame, removed a distracting compound-noun spelling issue, and clozed both fixed arms.

register: Neutral political and journalistic expression for taking part in a public demonstration against a measure, institution, or government.
trap: English protest covers both demonstrating and objecting verbally; French manifester guarantees public collective action, while protester may denote only an expressed objection.
example_tl: Dans plusieurs capitales, des étudiants ont manifesté contre la censure malgré les arrestations préventives et la présence massive de policiers en uniforme.
example_en: In several capitals, students protested against censorship despite preventive arrests and the massive presence of uniformed police officers.
cloze: Dans plusieurs capitales, des étudiants {{c1::ont manifesté contre}} la censure malgré les arrestations préventives et la présence massive de policiers en uniforme.
note: The English prompt is ambiguous. Guided by the political topic, self-review selected public demonstration; old_back’s protester remains valid for the narrower act of voicing an objection.

register: Neutral-formal expression for openly stating disagreement with a position, decision, doctrine, or institutional consensus.
trap: Standard France French normally paraphrases the verb; dissidence is a noun for more sustained or organized opposition and cannot translate the verbal prompt by itself.
example_tl: Trois membres du comité ont exprimé leur désaccord avec la doctrine officielle, au risque de compromettre leur carrière diplomatique.
example_en: Three committee members dissented from the official doctrine, at the risk of jeopardizing their diplomatic careers.
cloze: Trois membres du comité {{c1::ont exprimé leur désaccord avec}} la doctrine officielle, au risque de compromettre leur carrière diplomatique.
note: Materially corrects old_back, which supplies a noun instead of a production-ready verbal expression. Self-review chose an overt speech-act sense rather than the weaker être en désaccord.

register: Neutral-formal transitive verb when an authority forces someone to live outside their country or customary place of residence.
trap: Exiler is transitive and assigns agency to the authority; s’exiler makes the displaced person the subject and may describe a constrained or voluntary departure.
example_tl: Après le procès, le régime a exilé plusieurs intellectuels influents, espérant ainsi priver l’opposition de relais crédibles auprès des médias étrangers.
example_en: After the trial, the regime exiled several influential intellectuals, hoping thereby to deprive the opposition of credible contacts in foreign media.
cloze: Après le procès, le régime {{c1::a exilé}} plusieurs intellectuels influents, espérant ainsi priver l’opposition de relais crédibles auprès des médias étrangers.
note: Old_back is accurate for the transitive reading. Self-review excluded s’exiler from alts because its change of subject and agency prevents direct interchangeability in the example.

register: Neutral-formal construction for deterring an actor from an action; in strategy, the related doctrine is la dissuasion.
trap: French requires both the person deterred and de before an infinitive: dissuader les dirigeants de reprendre, not a direct calque without de.
example_tl: La perspective de sanctions coordonnées devait dissuader les dirigeants de reprendre les essais, sans toutefois leur offrir une voie de sortie négociée.
example_en: The prospect of coordinated sanctions was meant to deter the leaders from resuming the tests, without offering them a negotiated way out.
cloze: La perspective de sanctions coordonnées devait {{c1::dissuader}} les dirigeants {{c1::de}} reprendre les essais, sans toutefois leur offrir une voie de sortie négociée.
note: Old_back gives the correct verb but omits its two-part government. Self-review clozed both fixed arms and avoided empêcher, which would imply successful prevention rather than deterrence.

register: Neutral-formal transitive verb for increasing the intensity of a conflict, crisis, or campaign; the intransitive counterpart is s’intensifier.
trap: Escalader normally means to climb or scale a physical obstacle; escalader un conflit is an avoidable English calque in careful France French.
example_tl: La livraison de missiles supplémentaires a intensifié le conflit, réduisant les possibilités de négociation et augmentant le risque d’une intervention directe des superpuissances.
example_en: The delivery of additional missiles escalated the conflict, reducing the possibilities for negotiation and increasing the risk of direct superpower intervention.
cloze: La livraison de missiles supplémentaires {{c1::a intensifié}} le conflit, réduisant les possibilités de négociation et augmentant le risque d’une intervention directe des superpuissances.
note: Materially corrects old_back’s escalader. Dictionary review confirmed that the figurative strategic sense belongs to escalade, not the standard verb; self-review selected the transitive conflict sense.

register: Neutral-formal to specialist verb for rapid, often undesirable multiplication or spread; common in arms-control and security analysis.
trap: French proliférer is intransitive: programs or weapons prolifèrent; to express an external cause, use favoriser la prolifération rather than proliférer quelque chose.
example_tl: Après la rupture du traité, les programmes clandestins ont proliféré, compliquant les efforts internationaux de vérification et affaiblissant le régime de non-prolifération.
example_en: After the treaty collapsed, clandestine programs proliferated, complicating international verification efforts and weakening the non-proliferation regime.
cloze: Après la rupture du traité, les programmes clandestins {{c1::ont proliféré}}, compliquant les efforts internationaux de vérification et affaiblissant le régime de non-prolifération.
note: Old_back is accurate. Self-review made the intransitive restriction explicit and retained se multiplier because it can replace the main verb in this example after normal inflection.

register: Neutral and idiomatic for political, economic, or institutional change when both the starting point and destination are stated.
trap: Do not mechanically render a generic economic or policy transition as transitionner; careful standard prose prefers passer de … à … or a construction with the noun transition.
example_tl: Après 1989, plusieurs États sont passés d’une économie planifiée à une économie de marché sans construire immédiatement des institutions de régulation solides.
example_en: After 1989, several states transitioned from a planned economy to a market economy without immediately building robust regulatory institutions.
cloze: Après 1989, plusieurs États {{c1::sont passés d’}}une économie planifiée {{c1::à}} une économie de marché sans construire immédiatement des institutions de régulation solides.
note: Materially corrects old_back, which supplies only the noun transition. Self-review selected a two-endpoint verbal frame, replaced the vague modèle de marché, and clozed each fixed arm separately.
